findings.title: Distinguish constant charge amounts from fixed charge positions
findings.candidateQuote: In an electrostatic model with fixed charges
findings.approvedChineseCondition: The amounts of electric charge remain unchanged while relative positions may change.
findings.judgment: Fixed charges can mean charges held at fixed positions. That reading conflicts with the preceding change of relative positions and does not unambiguously retain the approved constant-charge-amount condition. This is a new-English wording defect, not a rejection or replay of the approved Chinese model.
findings.necessaryCorrection: Replace 'with fixed charges' with 'in which the amounts of electric charge remain constant', or equally explicit wording. Preserve the system-level energy assignment and the statement that it is not an isolated charge's own property.

findings.title: Express local field mediation without implying a short-range electric force
findings.candidateQuote: The original textbook uses the "short-range action" viewpoint
findings.approvedChineseMeaning: The historical viewpoint is explained as a charge experiencing force through the electric field at its own location.
findings.judgment: Short-range action introduces a range-related reading that the approved local-field explanation does not assert. Even though the remainder of the sentence explains the field at the charge's location, an independent young reader can interpret the named viewpoint as a restriction on how far electric forces act. This is a terminology-clarity defect in the English, not a fresh historical-source or science adjudication.
findings.necessaryCorrection: Use 'local-action viewpoint' or 'local field-action viewpoint' and keep the existing explanation that the electric field at the charge's location exerts the force. An explicit paraphrase of that local mediation is also acceptable; do not introduce a finite-range claim.

scienceChecks.judgment: Electrostatic potential energy is explicitly assigned to the interacting system and charge-field-source interaction, not to an isolated charge. The fixed external electrostatic field, moving test charge, negligible source disturbance, neglected radiation, self-field effects and medium changes are all retained. EN-01 and EN-02 must clarify the two English phrases without changing those approved conditions.

Atomic and chemical binding involve electromagnetic interactions with a complete quantum description required. Reactor energy is not presented as depletion of stored electrostatic energy: the historical attribution is identified as oversimplified, strong-interaction nuclear binding is acknowledged, and initial/final rest-energy differences can become kinetic energy and heat. No unsupported nuclear value, equation, or new energy-release claim is added.

Large parallel plates yield an approximate uniform central field away from edges, with plate charges held in their distribution. B is negative on the left, D positive on the right, field leftward, point 1 farther from B than point 2, both on one field line. The first moving charge is explicitly positive; E in the work expression is magnitude, so leftward displacement gives positive A=qE(d1-d2). The near-Earth gravity analogy retains its limited scope.

Perpendicular step segments do zero electric work. Along/against-field displacements enter with opposite signs, and the algebraic horizontal sum, not total unsigned staircase length, equals d1-d2. The staircase approximates an arbitrary smooth curve for calculation and is expressly not the particle's physical trajectory.

Conservative electrostatic work is the negative of the corresponding energy change, A=-Delta EP. The preserved chain qE(d1-d2)=-(qEd2-qEd1)=-(EP2-EP1) has correct signs. EP=qEd uses the negative plate as zero and d measured from it; the earlier positive-work example does not impose a positive-q restriction on the general signed-charge formula.

Potential-to-kinetic conversion is conditional on only the electric force doing work and neglected transfers such as radiation. Positive charge moving against the field gives negative electric work and increased potential energy, with kinetic energy decreasing under the same assumptions. Deceleration is not immediate stopping. Vacuum/picture-tube examples remain historical applications, and high-voltage DIY operation is explicitly forbidden.

The fixed electrostatic-field limitation remains in the closed-path argument. Return to the original position restores the same interaction potential energy, and the exact repeated-endpoint expression gives zero total electric work. No induced-field generalization is introduced.

An arbitrary reference at distance d0 is explicitly allowed, rather than requiring the plate as zero. EP=qEd-qEd0 gives zero there and changes the energy by a position-independent constant for the same field-source model. Forces, work and energy differences remain unchanged; the absolute numerical value depends on the chosen zero. The wording avoids the historical blanket claim that potential energy has no meaning.

Unlike mass, charge q can be negative. With the negative-plate zero and nonnegative distance, q<0 gives negative potential energy between the plates away from the zero, and zero remains zero. Negative potential energy is not negative kinetic energy or a violation of conservation.
